comments.body: Hi jinchenglee nice project I think that if you look at equation 3 in page 4 in the paper the gradients with respect to each conv layer are spatially averaged for each feature map i Is there a chance you were confusing w c k in equation 1 that is used in case of regular CAM Here is another way to verify that the result is like in the paper They state that in case of a model that has global average pooling a dense layer the output of grad cam and that of the older CAM algorithm is identical when creating visualizations for the last conv layer Grad CAM is designed to have this property In case of the older CAM visualization the weight w i at index i in the final dense layer corresponding to some class C is used to multiply A i the conv layer output before the global average pooling Now lets look at grad cam when using this same architecture The gradient of the loss L with respect to A i in the feature map is w i since the loss is a sum over w i A i The spatial average of the gradients for all the pixels is also w i since the gradient is identical for every pixel Therefore grad cam and cam have the same result in this case
